Senior Instructors

OBJECTIVES

  • At the end of this course participants should be able to understand:
  • Role on Monday evenings
  • Reasonable adjustment pathway students - teaching and examining
  • Kit issues and troubleshooting
  • Grey areas and supporting instructors
  • Research opportunities and wider involvement with RMD

To note

Explanation of changes + RCUK Check Call CPR

Monday Nights

  • Support teaching in rooms
  • 1-to-1 teaching with struggling candidates
  • RAP teaching
  • Liaise with Student Faculty
Encouragement of checklist use and empowering assessors to request replacement equipment if any concerns e.g. non-sticky pads, low AED batteries. Debate RE whether to have assistant step out for verdict (previous consensus that does not need to be routine practice)

Grey areas and common questions

  • Poor head tilt chin lift + inadequate rescue breaths
  • No pinch of nose during breaths
  • Candidate pausing CPR when assistant offers them help
  • Not checking for response/breathing before or after recovery position
  • A few candidates are unaware they are expected to do the full run-through
  • Staring at examiner during shock

Reasonable Adjustment Pathway (RAP) students

  • Students who are unable to complete a standard BLS examination for medical or other reason
  • Must be discussed with Student Faculty
  • Examples
  • Unable to do chest compressions
  • Manikin on table etc
Discussions around opening gambit, explanation of phone/tablet/laptop use (and context RE mistaken QCPR), discussion around verdict delivery and avoiding delaying verdict or giving too much feedback.

Kit issues and troubleshooting

  • Instructors should notify you of issues with kit
  • New kit provided if you deem necessary
  • Examples
  • AEDs - battery pack
  • Manikins - chest not inflating

Challenging students

  • Refusal to get involved in teaching rooms
  • Take out and try 1-1 teaching
  • Escalation
  • Calm but firm - necessity of degree
Discussion/debate RE how to delivery unsuccessful verdict, discussion RE focussing on most salient fail points (and context of complaints where candidate has latched on to minor issue mentioned first), discussion RE what to do with candidate when fail verdict given, discussion RE having assistant step outside for verdict or not.

Exam nights

  • 2 to be allocated to pre-exam teaching
  • 6 to be allocated to re-sit teaching
  • Cover absences and examine if necessary
Discussion/debate RE how to delivery unsuccessful verdict, discussion RE focussing on most salient fail points (and context of complaints where candidate has latched on to minor issue mentioned first), discussion RE what to do with candidate when fail verdict given, discussion RE having assistant step outside for verdict or not.

Research opportunities and wider involvement with RMD

  • Research across the RMD UK network
  • Original research into near-peer BLS teaching and assessment began at RMD Birmingham
  • Over twenty peer-reviewed papers since 1995; work continues across sites, supported by regular cross-site meetings
  • Wider involvement
  • Community teaching: school pupils, University staff and students, community events
  • Development Fund for CPD, and future roles within RMD

SUMMARY

  • Arrive on time
  • Re-familiarise with grey areas before assessment night
  • Avoid having document open during exams (or WhatsApp messages mid-exam)
  • Standardised approach
  • Feel empowered to fail borderline/poor performance
  • Student/Senior Faculty will support your decision making
  • Document fail reasons well on exam form
  • Raise recurrent issues. Repeated issues are fed back to instructors
  • This feedback has been instrumental in improving candidate performance
